# pass-style shorthand: an argument that is not a subcommand falls through to
# `show`, flags included. A bare `sesam` still prints the help, and a real
# subcommand always wins over a secret of the same name.

env CLIPBOARD_FILE=$WORK/clipboard
env SESAM_CLIPBOARD_COPY_CMD=$WORK/copy.sh
env SESAM_CLIPBOARD_PASTE_CMD=$WORK/paste.sh
env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=$WORK/run
mkdir $WORK/run
chmod 0755 $WORK/copy.sh
chmod 0755 $WORK/paste.sh
chmod 0755 $WORK/clear.sh

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

exec sesam add pw.txt --group dev

# Bare `sesam` prints the root help, not show's - the command list is the
# whole point of it.
exec sesam
stdout 'Manage encrypted secrets in git repositories'
stdout 'SECRETS'
! stdout 'sesam show - '

# Only global flags is still no request to show anything.
exec sesam --quiet
stdout 'Manage encrypted secrets in git repositories'

# `sesam show` on its own asks about show, so it gets show's help.
exec sesam show
stdout 'sesam show - '
! stdout 'Manage encrypted secrets in git repositories'

# A path falls through to show.
exec sesam pw.txt
stdout 's3cr3t'

# ... and so do show's flags, on either side of the implied command name.
exec sesam -c --ttl 0 pw.txt
! stdout .
grep '^s3cr3t$' $WORK/clipboard

exec $WORK/clear.sh
exec sesam --ttl 0 -c pw.txt
! stdout .
grep '^s3cr3t$' $WORK/clipboard

# The explicit form keeps working unchanged.
exec $WORK/clear.sh
exec sesam show -c --ttl 0 pw.txt
! stdout .
grep '^s3cr3t$' $WORK/clipboard

# A real subcommand is never shadowed, even by a secret of the same name.
exec sesam add status --group dev
exec sesam status
stdout 'in sync'
! stdout 'i am not the status command'

-- pw.txt --
s3cr3t
-- status --
i am not the status command
-- copy.sh --
#!/bin/sh
cat > "$CLIPBOARD_FILE"
-- paste.sh --
#!/bin/sh
cat "$CLIPBOARD_FILE" 2>/dev/null
-- clear.sh --
#!/bin/sh
: > "$CLIPBOARD_FILE"
